title: Flutter web Shader compilation error
body: I have a Flutter web app using the CanvasKit renderer. When I build it with `flutter build web --web-renderer canvaskit` and publish it to Firebase Hosting, the page does not work and Chrome DevTools shows a shader compilation error. The same app works in debugging mode. I expect the published website to render normally.

symptoms_visible: The published CanvasKit website does not render and Chrome DevTools reports a shader compilation error, while the app works in debugging mode.
N0.label: N0 published CanvasKit failure reported

symptoms_visible: The hosted site fails in Chrome Beta 121 on an Intel Mac, but works in other tested browsers, Chrome Stable 120, and Chrome Canary 122.
N1.label: N1 browser and architecture scope identified

symptoms_visible: A release build from the Flutter master channel shows the same blank-page failure, and the problem occurs with CanvasKit rather than the HTML renderer.
N2.label: N2 Flutter channel and renderer scope confirmed

symptoms_visible: The console reports `CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL`, followed by a shader compilation error containing a fragment shader with circle-related uniforms.
The failure remains after reducing the app to a list of circular avatars.
An engineer reproduces a GPU-process crash on an Intel Mac when Chrome uses ANGLE's Metal backend.
N3.label: N3 shader evidence and ANGLE-Metal reproduction collected

symptoms_visible: Enabling `Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization` helps some affected machines, but another affected Intel Mac still fails after trying it, and the reporter cannot require customers with a blank page to change Chrome flags.
N4_x.label: N4_x Chrome flag workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: On affected Intel Macs, loading a network JPG or JPEG in a release CanvasKit app makes the page fail, while equivalent PNG, WebP, and GIF images render.
Multiple users reproduce the hosted example in Chrome 121 or 122 on Intel macOS, while the same app works on Apple Silicon or in Safari.
N4.label: N4 JPEG trigger isolated across affected users

symptoms_visible: The same release app renders successfully when built with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false`; normal browser image decoding still triggers the failure on the affected configuration.
N5.label: N5 Flutter-side mitigation verified

symptoms_visible: After updating Chrome to a build containing the Chromium-side rollback, the hosted CanvasKit example renders again for the reporter and other previously affected Intel Mac users.
N6.label: N6 Chromium fix verified by affected users

symptoms_visible: Updated Chrome versions render the published CanvasKit application and its network JPEG images normally on the previously affected Intel Macs.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved by Chromium rollout

question_patterns: Does the hosted site fail in another browser?
Which exact Chrome version and Mac architecture reproduce the problem?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It works in all the browsers I tried except Chrome Beta 121.0.6167.16 x86_64 on my 2020 Intel MacBook Pro.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails in every browser and on both Intel and Apple Silicon machines.
It reproduces in a slightly newer Chrome 121 beta build on the same Intel Mac.

question_patterns: Can you compare Chrome Stable, Beta, and Canary on the same machine?
Do adjacent Chrome versions reproduce the failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the same Intel macOS machine, Chrome Stable 120 works, Chrome Beta 121 fails, and Chrome Canary 122 works.

edges.comment: Browser comparison narrowed the initial failure to a particular Chrome channel and Intel macOS rather than all published Flutter web builds.

question_patterns: Can you test the app using the Flutter master channel?
Please build on master and provide the `flutter doctor -v` output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Flutter master 3.18.0-18.0.pre.39 produces the same result on the Intel Mac.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is already fixed when the app is built from Flutter master.

question_patterns: Does this only occur with the CanvasKit renderer?
Does an HTML-renderer build show the same failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it occurs only with CanvasKit rendering.

edges.comment: Testing master ruled out an already-landed Flutter fix, while the renderer comparison localized the visible failure to the CanvasKit path.

question_patterns: Please provide the failing browser's `about:gpu` output and the console error as text.
Can you paste the complete shader compilation log rather than a screenshot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The GPU report shows hardware-accelerated WebGL and the console logs `CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL`, an invalid delete operation, and a fragment shader compilation error containing `ucircle_S1_c0`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The console contains only an HTTP 404 for an application asset and no WebGL context loss or shader error.
The same shader text is printed with different DevTools line wrapping.

question_patterns: Can you reduce the reproduction further?
What is the smallest remaining widget tree that still triggers the error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I removed the extra code and kept only `UserStories()`, a list of circular avatars, and the published site still produces the same error.

edges.comment: The collected log enabled an engineer to reproduce a GPU-process crash with ANGLE's Metal backend and infer that the failing shader came from Skia inside Chrome's HTML rasterization path, not Flutter's bundled CanvasKit shaders.

solution.intent: Treat enabling Chrome's `Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization` flag as the resolution for affected users.
solution.concrete_example: Open `chrome://flags`, enable `Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization`, relaunch Chrome, and consider the issue solved.

edges.comment: This was an actual suggestion in the thread. It helped some machines, but one affected user reported that it did not work, and the reporter rejected requiring production customers to edit browser flags. Multi-user evidence is folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you isolate which image or widget property triggers the crash?
Does the failure depend on loading a particular network image format?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A minimal release app using `Image.network` fails when the URL returns JPG or JPEG. Removing the network JPEG makes the app work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The app still fails with no images at all, and a plain colored box triggers the same crash.
A different network JPEG URL reproduces the same failure.

question_patterns: What happens if the same test uses PNG, WebP, or GIF instead of JPEG?
Can you compare several image formats in the minimal reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: PNG, WebP, and GIF network images work in the same example; JPG is the format that reliably causes the shader failure.

question_patterns: Can anyone else reproduce the hosted example, and on what hardware and browser?
Is this consistently limited to Chrome on Intel Macs?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Several affected users reproduce the same blank page and shader error in Chrome 121 or 122 on Intel Macs. The same versions work on Apple Silicon, and Safari works on the affected Intel machines.

edges.comment: Reports from multiple affected users are merged into one simulated user side. Their format comparisons isolated browser-decoded network JPEGs as a reliable trigger.

question_patterns: Can you compile the release app with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` and test it?
Does disabling browser image decoding prevent the JPEG-triggered crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Building with `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false` makes the release app work on the affected Intel Mac.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The build still crashes with exactly the same JPEG shader error after browser image decoding is disabled.

question_patterns: Is there a downside to keeping browser image decoding disabled?
Can this build option be used as a permanent fix without performance impact?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is usable as a temporary mitigation, but images are decoded on the UI thread, so many, large, or animated images may cause jank.

edges.comment: This is a handler-initiated configuration probe, so it is represented as clarification only. It confirmed that Chrome's browser image-decoding path was involved and provided a temporary Flutter-side mitigation.

question_patterns: What did Chromium change for affected Intel Macs?
Has the Chrome-side ANGLE-Metal experiment been rolled back or disabled?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Chromium disabled the ANGLE-on-Metal experiment on Intel Macs and rolled the change out in an updated Chrome build.

question_patterns: After updating Chrome, does the original hosted reproduction work without changing Flutter or browser flags?
Can affected Intel Mac users verify the Chromium rollout?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Chrome 122.0.6261.129 renders the site again for me, and other previously affected users confirm that it works for them too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The updated Chrome build still crashes and `chrome://gpu` shows ANGLE Metal is disabled.
The same fix is verified in a slightly newer patched Chrome build.

edges.comment: Affected users tested the Chrome build containing the Chromium-side rollback. The reporter and additional users verified the original production reproduction before closure.

solution.intent: Resolve the incident through Chromium's rollout disabling the faulty ANGLE-Metal path on Intel Macs, advise affected users to update Chrome, and retain Flutter build options only as temporary mitigations.
solution.concrete_example: This is a Chromium ANGLE/Metal regression on Intel macOS, not a shader authored by the Flutter app. Chrome's browser-side Skia path can crash while compiling a shader when rasterizing browser-decoded JPEG content. Chromium disabled the ANGLE-Metal experiment for Intel Macs; update to a Chrome build containing that rollback and verify the hosted app. Until the update reaches users, `--dart-define=BROWSER_IMAGE_DECODING_ENABLED=false`, non-JPEG formats, the HTML renderer, or selecting OpenGL may mitigate the issue, with the documented performance or deployment tradeoffs.

edges.comment: The issue was closed only after Chromium rolled out its Intel Mac ANGLE-Metal rollback and the reporter plus other affected users confirmed that the original hosted reproduction worked again.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the true root cause as a Chromium ANGLE-on-Metal regression on Intel macOS that crashes the GPU process while Chrome's Skia/HTML rasterization path compiles a shader; the failing shader is not application shader code or a shader supplied by Flutter's CanvasKit copy.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: Intel macOS and Chrome specificity, WebGL context loss and shader log, engineer reproduction with ANGLE Metal, the reliable network-JPEG trigger, and success when browser image decoding is disabled.

Must not present enabling `Out-of-process 2D canvas rasterization` as the production resolution: it did not work for one affected user and requiring customers to change `chrome://flags` was explicitly rejected. Other Flutter-side workarounds must be described as temporary and include their tradeoffs.
Must resolve through the Chromium rollout disabling or reverting ANGLE Metal on Intel Macs, with affected users updating Chrome rather than requiring a Flutter framework patch.
Must not declare the issue resolved until the reporter and other previously affected users verify that the original hosted CanvasKit application works in the updated Chrome build.

persona_hint.experience_level: Intermediate Flutter developer who can publish minimal web reproductions, switch Flutter channels and renderers, inspect Chrome GPU diagnostics and console logs, test build-time defines, and reduce a widget tree, but relies on browser and engine specialists for graphics-pipeline diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative, direct, and persistent; provides exact versions and test results, follows requested diagnostics, proposes hypotheses, and pushes back when a workaround cannot realistically be imposed on production customers.
